decisions.reason: The address autocomplete web service draws on the firm's existing address and grid databases at low marginal cost, and with the firm expanding and holding slack there is no performance shortfall that would trigger problemistic search to drop it.

The Austrian gas grid fee database extends the core fee-data competence into a neighbouring market, but its smaller customer base makes it the likeliest to fall below aspiration; slack still lets the firm carry it while results remain uncertain.
Determining peak load windows is a regulated, recurring need of network operators that fits the firm's process-based platform direction, so it plausibly meets its aspiration level.
An end-customer tariff database sits at the heart of the firm's market-data business and supports its platform strategy, making withdrawal unlikely.
Custom web services are a flexible offering that matches the move toward standardized data exchange and SaaS, and they tie up few dedicated resources.
The postal code lookup service is a low-cost companion to the address services; it might be merged into a broader offering, but there is no clear shortfall to justify dropping it.
